title: Kernel mini-triage scratch
content:
2024-11-08 morning dump - quick personal triage

Context: quick scratch for today's kernel-level perf blips on staging. Not a polished write-up; jotting hypotheses and steps so I don't forget between meetings.

Summary of problem:
- p99 token latency spikes on small-chat workload during autoscale events (burst to 50 qps). Baseline p99 ~125ms, spikes to ~210-320ms for ~30s windows.
- Repro pattern: warm cache, then sudden concurrent prefix hits + metronome rhythm misalignment (we suspect batch scheduler + KV cache eviction).

Observed signals (staging monitors):
- metric: inference.p99.tokens - baseline 125ms -> spike 310ms at 09:12
- node-level: CPU steal on host-gpu-12 ~3-5% at same time, but not enough to explain full delta
- nvlink/util: steady, GPU utilization stable ~42%
- runtime logs: many `kv_cache: miss` followed by `kv_cache: load_from_disk` for same prefix id (~20% of misses during window)
- kernel: dmesg shows repeated softirq warnings around 09:11 (likely network RX bursts)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV cache eviction race: eviction policy triggers disk fetch for the same prefix concurrently -> many requests block on disk IO and stall metronome batches.
2) Batch scheduler jitter: metronome alignment combined with autoscale causes transient batch size drop and many small batches -> increased overhead per token.
3) Network RX bursts cause softirq backlog -> threads get preempted briefly affecting scheduler wakeups.
4) NUMA migration + buffer reallocation on specific hosts (less likely but saw a couple of numa-bound kernels in trace).

Quick reproduction steps (local/staging):
- repro script: scripts/repro/kvconcur_burst.py (simulate 50 qps burst with repeated same-prefix tokens)
- reproduce command: PYTHONPATH=. python3 scripts/repro/kvconcur_burst.py --qps 50 --duration 60 --prefix-id test_xx
- capture traces: run with SAMPLER=1 to get tracer output to /tmp/trace.json

Things I ran today (notes):
- ran repro on staging-2, got p99 ~290ms, saw `load_from_disk` spikes matching earlier logs.
- loaded /proc/sched debug info (echo 1 > /proc/sys/kernel/sched_debug) and snapshot of per-thread runqueue times.
- small perf: `perf top -p <server-pid>` during spike: top shows kernel lock contention around `fsync` path in our disk-backed cache loader.

Immediate mitigations to try (fast):
- change eviction policy to avoid immediate disk load for hot prefixes: add short-lived in-memory tombstone for recently-evicted keys (cheap TTL 2s) -> prevents stampede. (owner: Kiara, est: 2-3h)
- throttle concurrent disk loads: semaphore limiting parallel disk fetches (owner: Omar, est: 3-5h)
- metronome tuning: quick experiment reduce jitter tolerance to align batches less aggressively during scale events (owner: Lina, est: 2h)

Longer-term/engineering tasks:
- rewrite disk loader to use async io (aio) path to avoid kernel fsync stalls; ticket RINF-3498 opened. (owner: infra team, est: spike 2d)
- add KV cache read-through instrumentation: tag requests that caused disk IO and trace back request ids (owner: Kiara/Omar, est: 1d)
- test under packet burst using netem to validate softirq hypothesis (owner: SRE, est: 1d)

Notes to self / TODOs:
- [ ] Push a small semaphore patch to branch 'kv-guard' and run in canary (PR draft started).
- [ ] Add additional logging around `kv_cache: load_from_disk` to include stack hash and time-since-evict. Short-term keep logs at debug level in staging only.
- [ ] Coordinate with SRE to run netem test in staging around off-peak to simulate RX burst; link: Jira RINF-3421.
- [ ] Validate whether disk latencies correlate with kernel softirq events (collect `irqbalance` logs + iostat).
- [ ] Check metronome commit history for recent change (see PR #823) - maybe revert the micro-optimizations if they introduced alignment fragility.

Useful commands I ran / will run:
- repro: PYTHONPATH=. python3 scripts/repro/kvconcur_burst.py --qps 50 --duration 60 --prefix-id test_xx
- capture trace: SAMPLER=1 ./bin/runtime --config staging.conf 2>&1 | tee /tmp/runtime.log
- perf: sudo perf record -F 99 -p <pid> -g -- sleep 30; sudo perf report --stdio | head -n 40
- iostat snapshot: iostat -x 1 10 > /tmp/iostat-$(date +%s).log

Mini design note (sketch for semaphore patch):
- create global limiter keyed by prefix-shard; each in-memory fetch path does: if try_acquire(limit) then load-from-disk else return fallback (serve stale cache or requeue to retry with small jitter).
- fallback behavior: return last-known prefix tokens with small extra latency and instrument as `served-stale`. Avoid blocking request path on disk.
- risk: slight quality/regression in rare cases -> wrap with feature flag and roll out to 10% canary.

Follow-ups after patch merge:
- run synthetic burst tests x10 (qps 50/100) and verify p99 reduction during autoscale windows
- add a regression alert if p99 > 200ms for 2m window post-rollout (build on existing datadog monitor)

Random quick thoughts:
- Could we do a probabilistic negative caching: after eviction, mark key "likely cold" and serve from compressed KV for 1s without disk fetch? probably more complexity.
- Consider moving hot-prefix metadata into RAM-only small LRU (size 512) to avoid disk trip entirely for popular prefixes.

Meeting notes to paste into ticket later:
- Omar: will prototype semaphore and test on canary; Lina: metronome tuning and batch-stability tests; SRE: netem test scheduled Thursday night.

End-of-day: leave this doc as single source-of-truth for quick followups. Will convert to PR checklist once semaphore patch is green.

-- Kiara
